description: REGENERATED FROM THE AUTHORITATIVE M6 PHASE C WORK ORDER (not a verbatim recovery of the lost original). WALL Android driver: epoch/elapsed anchor, wallGeneration, timer ticket, fresh clock evaluation, clock drift/reanchor, bounded wait with Android signals. The driver samples the OS civil time and monotonic clock, maintains an in-memory-only anchor, schedules at most one bounded local wake, re-reads fresh civil time on every callback before deciding DUE, detects drift/jumps and reanchors, and feeds fresh-epoch evaluations into the pure WallCalendarScheduler. The driver is NEW Android code that lives OUTSIDE the pure wall/ package (so the Phase B purity gate still passes) and drives the common owner from FEAT-002. It MUST NOT modify the Phase B WallCalendarScheduler (which stays payload-free and clock-free). Covers Phase C scope items 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and the driver/race portions of 13, 14.
steps: Read docs/scenevibe-os-m6-banner-wall-clock-architecture.md sections 3 (temporal authority & anchor), 5 (deterministic WALL semantics), 13 (owner thread/generations/races), 14 (clock-jump policy), 15 (bounded diagnostics) before implementing. Note the exact constants PROPOSED there and treat them as the spec to test: elapsed read window <= 50 ms, at most 2 immediate retries before fail-closed, drift >= 1000 ms invalidates the anchor, single wait = min(next WALL boundary, 1000 ms), no zero-delay loop.

Add the Android WALL driver class(es) in app/src/main/java/com/scenevibe/tvcompanionpoc/ (NOT under wall/). The driver: samples epoch via System.currentTimeMillis() bracketed by SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() before/after (reject incoherent sample / decreasing counter / read interval > 50 ms, at most two immediate retries then fail closed); builds an in-memory Anchor{epochUtc, referenceElapsed, activationToken, wallGeneration}; uses anchorEpoch+elapsedDelta ONLY to prepare a wait and measure drift, never to decide DUE. Keep the civil-time source and monotonic source injectable (interface seams) so the driver is JVM-testable with fake epoch/elapsed/uptime sources exactly as section 18 'Driver' gates require.

Schedule at most ONE wait at a time via Handler.postDelayed with a RELATIVE duration = min(scheduler.nextBoundaryEpochMs()-now, 1000 ms), never passing an elapsedRealtime value as an uptime timestamp to postAtTime (section 3). A boundary at exactly now is handled in the current evaluation, then the wait targets a strictly-future boundary. After horizon exhaustion the bounded <=1s check still allows re-evaluation on a backward clock correction without creating new occurrences (diagnostic WALL_HORIZON_EXHAUSTED).

Guard every callback with wallGeneration + a unique timer ticket + the active activation token. On fire: verify ticket+generation+token are current (else NO-OP even if Android still delivered the runnable), re-read a FRESH civil-time sample, then call scheduler.evaluate(freshEpoch, eligible) synchronously and forward at most one EXIT then one DUE to the common owner under the captured generation. Never re-queue a DUE computed before a clock correction; an old deadline never proves DUE by itself.

Implement clock-jump/reanchor policy (section 14): an absolute drift >= 1000 ms between fresh civil sample and monotonic projection invalidates the anchor; an explicit time-change / timezone-change / resume / service-reentry / wake signal forces re-evaluation even below threshold. A significant correction cancels the timer ticket, increments wallGeneration, takes a fresh anchor, and recomputes the current candidate (at most 256 windows, at most one EXIT+DUE). The captured manifest generation does NOT change on a clock correction (correcting a clock never reloads the manifest or retags an old callback). wallGeneration (temporal source guard) and the controller generation (manifest guard) are two distinct guards and must not be conflated.

Receive Android interactivity/time signals via a DYNAMIC receiver (ACTION_TIME_CHANGED / ACTION_TIMEZONE_CHANGED / SCREEN_ON/OFF as interactivity hints, resume) to trigger reanchor/re-evaluation and suspend+hide presentation on a local suspension signal, re-evaluating on return. Do NOT add AlarmManager-exact, any new permission, wake lock, process wake, or Direct Boot. If the process cannot run it displays nothing during that unavailability; a delayed-but-alive service shows only the still-active window on resume. A clock that cannot be read or is out of the valid domain masks and disarms the volatile path, keeps the durable, emits a bounded diagnostic (WALL_CLOCK_INVALID / WALL_DEADLINE_FAILED), and does NOT trigger a new commit or ACK.

Wire the driver to the common owner so the first WALL evaluation occurs ONLY after safe pending->active promotion (pending never renders); the wait registration for the next wake must have succeeded before the ARMED result, and an initial clock/registration error fails ARM closed. No WALL anchor / wallGeneration / timer ticket / consumed cursor is durable.

Add JVM tests (JUnit4) driving the driver with fake epoch/elapsed/uptime sources and a RecordingSink/common-owner fake: forward and backward jumps (+30min skips intermediate windows, -5min may re-show a window, no MEDIA-seek logic), drift just under/over 1000 ms, explicit signal forcing re-eval under threshold, deep-sleep inclusion in elapsed vs uptime exclusion, read interval > 50 ms rejected with bounded retries then fail-closed, decreasing elapsed rejected, cancelled callback delivered as NO-OP, replaced ticket neutralizes an old callback, generation/ticket overflow fails closed, process restart yields a fresh temporal context (no restored anchor). Assert the pure WallCalendarScheduler is used unchanged and that no DUE is emitted during pending. Keep app/.../wall/*.java and MediaCalendarScheduler byte-unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: The Android WALL driver lives OUTSIDE the pure wall/ package; app/src/main/java/.../wall/*.java remain byte-unchanged and still pass the Phase B purity gate (no android.*/System./Handler imports in wall/).

Every timer callback re-reads a fresh civil-time sample before deciding DUE; stale wallGeneration / stale timer ticket / stale activation token / cancelled callback are NO-OPs; the pure scheduler receives only fresh explicit epochs.

Anchor is in-memory only (epoch/elapsed/token/wallGeneration); drift >= 1000 ms or an explicit time/zone/resume/wake signal reanchors, cancels the ticket, bumps wallGeneration, and recomputes at most one EXIT+DUE; the captured manifest generation is unaffected by clock corrections.

At most one bounded wait (min(next boundary, 1000 ms)) is scheduled via postDelayed with a relative duration; no AlarmManager-exact, new permission, wake lock, or Direct Boot is introduced; an unreadable/out-of-domain clock masks+disarms the volatile path, keeps the durable, emits a bounded WALL diagnostic, and causes no commit/ACK.

The first WALL evaluation occurs only after promotion; wait registration must succeed before ARMED; no anchor/generation/ticket/cursor is durable; new JVM driver tests cover the section-14/section-18 driver matrix and pass (CI gate if no Android SDK).
verification: cd tests && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s . -p "test_*.py" (still 141 OK; pure WALL contract still 68/68 proving wall/ unchanged)

git diff --stat confirms app/src/main/java/.../wall/*.java and calendar/MediaCalendarScheduler.java unchanged; grep the new driver file(s) show android.os.Handler/SystemClock usage is in the driver, never in wall/

If an Android SDK can be provisioned under OPEN_INTERNET: Gradle :app:testDebugUnitTest --console=plain (new driver tests + all existing tests pass). Otherwise declare the Android unit figure as a CI-only gate honestly and rely on code review + host JVM verification of the injectable-source driver tests.

onSuspend hides + disarms, onResume re-evaluates the current window (reload at a fresh epoch so an identical eventId re-shows per section 6/22); horizon-exhausted keeps the bounded <=1s heartbeat (WALL_HORIZON_EXHAUSTED) so a backward correction can re-show a still-active window without creating a new occurrence; arm() runs the first WALL evaluation ONLY after the owner has safely promoted (it drives the owner's active token) and REQUIRES the single wait registration to succeed before returning ARMED (initial clock/registration error fails ARM closed); no AlarmManager-exact, new permission, wake lock, process wake or Direct Boot added.
